answer: A farm must thus either lie, which the juniper graph proves on replay, or recruit 90 outsiders whose stake is exposed alongside its own. Because the declaration is checked against funding history rather than taken on trust, the orchard registry records each claim and the signal audit publishes every slash. Attesters sign a declaration that they hold no common funding with the identity they attest, and a later finding of common funding voids the attestation and slashes 46% of the attester's bond. That is 26 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
